title: Connector Trust Model

tier_rules.rule: first-party code is reviewed as part of the application release
tier_rules.review: owner review, security gate, and regression evidence
tier_rules.visibility: visible to eligible local users after the application gate

tier_rules.rule: partner code stays scoped to an approved manifest and publisher
tier_rules.review: publisher identity, contract tests, security review, and recheck date
tier_rules.visibility: WITHHELD until authorized certification evidence exists
tier_rules.support: named partner owner plus core escalation

tier_rules.rule: community code is isolated and receives no implicit capability grant
tier_rules.review: automated contract checks and explicit operator review
tier_rules.visibility: local development visibility only; publication is deferred
tier_rules.support: community maintainer with incident escalation path

tier_rules.rule: local fixtures and mocks cannot make production or provider claims
tier_rules.review: developer-owned tests with an explicit non-production boundary
tier_rules.visibility: developer-only and never exposed as certified
tier_rules.support: local developer; no production support commitment

permission_defaults.secret_access: opaque references only; plaintext is DENIED

review_requirements.requirement: tier, publisher, capabilities, destinations, and support owner must be reviewed
review_requirements.evidence: committed manifest, deterministic contract tests, and dated review record

visibility.certified: LOCAL_ONLY until external authorization and evidence are present

support_owner.scope: triage, incident intake, disable, revoke, and audit handoff
support_owner.escalation: unresolved security or provider incidents escalate to the operator

revocation.trigger: policy violation, expired review, security incident, or operator request

claim_boundary: This local record defines trust policy; it does not certify, expose, install, execute, publish, or release a connector.
Trust tiers, permission defaults, review, visibility, support, and revocation are policy boundaries, not live provider observations.
Certification, provider exposure, external telemetry, signing, publication, and release remain DEFERRED-EXTERNAL.
